comments.value: I agree, but I know the devs just going to ignore and ban you.

They cant really outright ban clients because they are essentially mimicking the vrchat client, thats how they work. The ones that were getting banned were doing things that vrchat doesnt normally do and I assume that is how they detected it. Clients will never be fully preventable. But if they want to reduce the likely hood of people making them allowing modding is probably the best way. As well as doing server side verification of user actions to make sure they arent trying to exploit things.

Regardless of what the exact action is, some kind of decision needs to be made regarding mods. The issue is that a significant number of highly desired features that are absent from the game are driving people towards mods, and in ever greater numbers. It's creating a culture creep of widely discussed, shared and normalised modification. Whilst most of those mods might be perfectly benign, non-invasive and non-malicious, there are others that exist which do push the boundaries of what powers players should have, or otherwise are outright malicious. The culture around this is also a neighbour to modded-client use, and brings people closer to that highly undesirable side of the community. The more malicious client/mod use that exists, the more people who will be attracted/compelled to seek out their own clients for sake of protecting themselves and having a means to combat it, for lack of any other viable alternative. This in turn only escalates the entire situation, and turns things into some kind of ridiculous hacker arms race.
This problem really can't be understated. I've been under the impression that the current impending update from the VRC team is hopefully bringing some major reworks to networking and security, but regardless of if it is or isn't, it really needs to be a top priority for getting fixed ASAP.
Fix security. Fix the feature gap.

I feel that it is desirable to name it as an add-on system and use only those that have received official support.
After reviewing and accepting what has been posted, register the hash, refer to the hash, and eliminate mods that do not correspond (not approved).
You should also be able to turn add-ons on and off from within the advanced menu.

Pretty sure if VRC added a client scan so that every client must match their copy 1:1 in name and file size after each major update, there'd be a nice ban wave. Whether malicious or not. Plenty of games already do this. 
Pretty sure it's been the case that something similar has happened before. Just a heads up. The ban wave would continue until the mod makers patched their own mods or made them a third-party executable. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
But yes, official support somewhere down the line would be nice. I've been running vanilla in VRC for over 2 years without issue though. Impatience or entitlement are perfectly fine being punishable as things stand currently.

i believe mods is a nice idea for vrchat. but vrchat is just not secure enough to just let anyone use mods. why do you think they say it is ban-able for the use of any modification of the client? vrchat is way to unstable and not secure enough for this kind of implementation. they just added quest. which was a bad idea because there game is already unstable enough. now they have to add support for pc and vr and quest. don't get me wrong. i think it is always a good idea to add cross platform to games. but they added it way to soon.

most of the people I knew who were using mods were doing it for very specific reasons- finding people in huge maps (which if map makers would adopt the teleport menu from booth that would be far less of an issue) and having more avatar favorites (which vrc still just does not have anywhere near enough, and there's a lot of excellent or hilarious public models out there that don't have a corresponding avatar pedastal in a world somewhere).  Give people a better number of avatar favorites, and publicly encourage better teleport options in huge maps, and I'm willing to bet the majority of mod users would stop having a real use for them.

details: I'm not sure if custom client and mods are the same thing but I think it would be a good idea to allow for mods (perhaps in a controlled and secure system/environment) and remove all custom clients. Why allow mods? They bring so much new ideas, features, and value to the game. I highly encourage VRChat to enable the use of mods and remove the use of custom clients, especially malicious ones. I've been playing this game for many years now and it's become more of a lifestyle than a game. I've been playing with mods for a year now and I love the functionality they have to offer. I love the communities that are created to try new ideas and to collaborate with others. I disagree that people should be banned for having mods; especially right now where there is a ban wave. If users abuse the use of mods, then I agree they should be banned and the communities should be held liable to discourage this behavior and filter for users they can't trust. I believe there should be a security system where mods can be registered or used while ensuring the safety and security of other players (especially from obtaining and  ddosing with IPs). In conclusion, I hope that VRChat will support mods or use it as a platform in which to have feedback on features players would like to have in the future. Love VRChat and the community and lets find ways to improve the game we all love. Thank you.
title: No Custom Clients But Allow For Mods
